Metric: Where the board timer starts and stops
Softmax · 49 scores per row: HPS uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) to time command launch → completion polling → probability readback. Scores are already in the FPGA output buffer.
LayerNorm · 192 channels per token: HPS uses the same clock to time one batch launch → polling confirms in-place writeback is complete. Activations and coefficients are already staged. Verification readback happens afterward.

Softmax · 49 scores per row: The HPS starts and polls each row. Reading 49 × 1 byte took about 21 µs/row on the same FPGA image. With NEON enabled, 4 × 16-byte reads carry all 49 results, with padding in the last beat. That brought board time to about 5.09 µs/row.
LayerNorm · 192 channels per token: One HPS command covers 24 tokens. Results stay in the FPGA buffer, so launch and polling overhead is shared across the batch and there is no timed output readback.

Metric: Why INT8 is faster or slower on HPS
Softmax · 49 scores per row: The tested INT8 kernel uses a lookup table for exponentials. The FP32 baseline calls expf.
LayerNorm · 192 channels per token: INT8 stores inputs and outputs in 8 bits, but intermediate work uses 32- and 64-bit values. For each channel, INT8 must estimate or divide, correct the remainder, round, and saturate. For example, if 13 ÷ 4 is estimated as 4, the remainder 13 − 4 × 4 = −3 shows the quotient needs correction. FP32 avoids that per-channel integer correction and requantization.

Softmax · 49 scores per row: 5.8% vs. INT8, calculated as (5.404 − 5.088) ÷ 5.404. Fabric was faster in all five matched trials.
LayerNorm · 192 channels per token: 84.3% vs. exact-corrected INT8, calculated as (40.487 − 6.362) ÷ 40.487. Fabric was also 17.9% faster than FP32.
